messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Kannada, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |---|---|---| | Tant' | degree adverb marking the intensity of “bitter” | Kannada: ಇಷ್ಟು (isuṭṭu) as degree adverb before adjective; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | è | copular verb linking subject to predicate “bitter” | Kannada: ಇದೆ (ide) as present copula; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | amara | predicate adjective describing the subject’s bitterness | Kannada: ಕಹಿ (kahi) as predicative adjective; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | che | subordinator introducing comparative clause | Kannada: ಎಂದು (endu) as complementizer for clause; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | poco | degree adverb indicating “a little” in the comparison | Kannada: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ (svapla) as degree modifier of comparative; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | è | copular verb in comparative clause linking “death” to “more” | Kannada: ಇದೆ (ide) as present copula in comparative; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | più | comparative marker “more” | Kannada: ಹೆಚ್ಚು (hecchu) as comparative morpheme; Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | morte | standard of comparison “death” | Kannada: ಮರಣ (maraṇa) in ablative case with comparative marker (ಮರಣಕ್ಕಿಂತ); Back‑translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. | | ; | clause terminator | – | | ma | coordinating conjunction “but” | Kannada: ಆದರೆ (ādare) as contrastive conjunction; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | per | preposition introducing purpose infinitive | Kannada:ಗಾಗಿ (gāgi) as purpose postposition attached to infinitive; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | trattar | infinitive “to treat/discuss” | Kannada: ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು (carchisalu) infinitive verb with purpose marker; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | del | partitive/genitive “of the” | Kannada: ನಿಂದ (ninda) or ಗೆ (ge) depending on case; here use ನಿಂದ for “of the”; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | ben | abstract noun “good” | Kannada: ಉತ್ತಮ (uttama) as noun in genitive/partitive; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | ch' | relative pronoun “that” | Kannada: ಅದು (adu) as relative pronoun; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | i' | clitic pronoun “I” (subject) | Kannada: ನಾನು (nānu) as first‑person pronoun; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | vi | locative adverb “there” | Kannada: ಅಲ್ಲಿ (alli) as locative adverb; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | trovai | past tense “found” | Kannada: ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದೆ (kaṇḍuhiḍide) past perfect verb agreeing with subject; Back‑translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found. | | , | clause separator | – | | dirò | future tense “I will tell” | Kannada: ಹೇಳುವೆನು (hēḷuvēnu) future form with first‑person marker; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | de | preposition “of” | Kannada: ಬಗ್ಗೆ (bagge) as post‑position for “about”; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | l' | definite article “the” | Kannada: ಆ (ā) as demonstrative determiner; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | altre | attributive adjective “other” | Kannada: ಇತರ (itara) agreeing in number/gender; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | cose | plural noun “things” | Kannada: ವಿಷಯಗಳು (viṣayagaḷu) plural noun in accusative; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | ch' | relative pronoun “that” | Kannada: ಅವು (avu) as relative pronoun referring to “things”; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | i' | clitic pronoun “I” (subject) | Kannada: ನಾನು (nānu); Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | v' | locative adverb “there” | Kannada: ಅಲ್ಲಿ (alli); Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | ho | auxiliary “have” for perfect | Kannada: ಇದೆ (ide) as auxiliary for perfect aspect; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | scorte | past participle “seen” | Kannada: ಕಂಡ (kaṇḍa) participle agreeing with object; Back‑translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. | | . | sentence terminator | – |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Kannada. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Kannada text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #7 Target Text: ಇಷ್ಟು ಕಹಿ ಇದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಇದೆ; Back-Translation: It is so bitter that it is a little more than death. Reference Translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. Reference Translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. ```kannada ಇಷ್ಟು ಕಹಿ ಇದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಇದೆ; ಆದರೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲುಗಾಗಿ ನಿಂದ ಉತ್ತಮ ಅದು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದೆ, ಹೇಳುವೆನು ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಆ ಇತರ ವಿಷಯಗಳು ಅವು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿದೆ. ```
